lastCompletedStory.title: Review round 2 fix 001: address reviewer finding

openQuestions: Round-2 review finding at test/integration/orch-respawn-reresolve.test.ts:164 correctly showed round-1's fix (US-R1-001, raising only the outer per-test bun timeout to 20_000) could not have addressed the recorded 'invocations.length 1 instead of 2 with result.error undefined' symptom, since node:child_process spawnSync blocks the JS thread synchronously and bun's per-test timeout cannot preempt it mid-call (confirmed via WebSearch against Node/Bun subprocess-timeout semantics). This story raised both the inner spawnSync timeout and outer per-test timeout in step (25_000/30_000) and added stdout/stderr/status/signal to both tests' failure-diagnostic messages, but the ORIGINAL non-timeout root cause (why the bash respawn loop under src/commands/run.ts:388-460 would ever emit only 1 claude invocation with a clean exit) was NOT reproduced despite bounded empirical stress testing: repeated isolated bun test runs (15+) under 20-70 concurrent CPU-bound background processes (both sequential and parallel), plus one full bun run check:all run (test/coverage/skip-ratchet gates each execute the whole 5758-test suite sequentially, closely matching the originally-reported conditions) -- all green, 0 fail. If this specific test ever fails again with the SAME 'invocations.length mismatch, result.error undefined' shape, the now-attached stdout/stderr/status/signal diagnostic output should make root-causing it tractable without re-deriving from prose; if it recurs, treat it as a genuine defect per the no-flaky-evasion rule, not as environmental noise.
nextStoryContext: US-R2-001 closed the round-2 WARNING at test/integration/orch-respawn-reresolve.test.ts:164 (also flagging :143/:257/:334-336). The finding was a real logical defect in US-R1-001's flake mitigation: it raised ONLY the outer bun per-test timeout (5000->20_000) while leaving the inner spawnSync timeout at 15_000, and -- as this round's reviewer proved -- neither timeout budget was ever consistent with the originally-recorded failure symptom (result.error undefined, i.e. no timeout fired) in the first place, since spawnSync's synchronous blocking nature makes bun's async per-test timeout structurally unable to preempt it. Fix applied: both spawnSync timeouts raised 15_000->25_000, both per-test timeouts raised 20_000->30_000 (kept 'in step', per the reviewer's own explicitly sanctioned fallback), and both tests' result.error/invocations.length assertions now carry stdout/stderr/status/signal in their failure message via bun's expect(actual, message) second-arg form for future diagnosability. Comments at both trailing-comment blocks rewritten to state the correct mechanism (spawnSync's own timeout is the true governing budget) instead of the round-1 comment's inaccurate 'outer timeout races the inner one' framing. Root cause of the original 1-invocation flake was investigated at length (static trace of the whole bash respawn loop in buildOrchestratorPaneCommand, src/commands/run.ts:371-460 -- no timing-dependent branch found under the given test fixtures) and empirically (stress-tested under CPU contention, plus one real full bun run check:all run matching the original repro conditions) without reproducing it; documented honestly as an open question above rather than claimed-fixed. All quality gates green: bun run typecheck (0 errors), bun test (5758 pass / 0 fail across 343 files), bun run check:all (every gate ok, including the test/coverage/skip-ratchet gates that each run the full suite once more). This was the only passes:false story in prd.json before this run (jq confirms); the supervisor's terminal-verdict hook may file further round-3 fixes off any remaining review findings, or the PRD may now be complete.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Bun's own test-timeout docs don't document the interaction with a synchronous blocking spawnSync call; a follow-up WebSearch against Node/Bun subprocess-timeout issue trackers confirmed spawnSync blocks the JS thread synchronously (native waitpid-style wait), so bun's async per-test timeout cannot preempt it mid-call -- the spawnSync 'timeout' option is the only budget that actually governs such a test. This directly falsified round-1's (US-R1-001) theory that raising only the outer per-test timeout would fix the flake, and drove this story's fix of raising both budgets in step rather than the outer one alone.
